sections.content: How many people are "higher level teaching assistants"?

125,435 people

were counted on the census as "higher level teaching assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Higher level teaching assistants (HLTA�s) assist teachers with their day-to-day classroom work, and the provision and planning of lesson materials.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "higher level teaching assistants" there were more women than men (89.8% compared with 10.2%).

This means "higher level teaching assistants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health and social care associate professionals".

Men made up 10.2% and women made up 89.8% of "higher level teaching assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "higher level teaching assistants" included:

  • beauticians and related occupations
  • typists and related keyboard occupations
  • receptionists

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "higher level teaching assistants" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 45 to 49 years. Of the whole working population 11% were aged 45 to 49 years. For people working as "higher level teaching assistants", 14.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "higher level teaching assistants" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "higher level teaching assistants" included:

  • educational support assistants
  • vehicle paint technicians
  • youth and community workers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "higher level teaching assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "higher level teaching assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "higher level teaching assistants", 10.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (51.2% compared with 48.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.7%) than self-employed (1.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
